long_description:
We have a very special event to close the year.

WIFT NZ is delighted to welcome Oscar and BAFTA-winning costume designer Kate Hawley.

This year, Kate has won the following awards for her contribution to Guillermo del Toro's Frankenstein (2025)

Academy Award for Best Achievement in Costume Design

BAFTA for Best Costume Design

Critics Choice for Best Costume Design

Costume Designers Guild Awards for Excellence in Period Film

Plus 19 other awards around the globe!

She also received multiple nominations for Best Costume for Lord Of The Rings: Rings of Power (2022) and Crimson Peak (2015).

To top it all off, she also received the inaugural Costume Designer of the Year Award from the British Fashion Council. 

Hawley has been praised for her "...meticulous construction, narrative sensitivity and ability to elevate character through custom-built textiles and silhouettes. ...she has built an international career across film, opera, theatre and ballet. Her credits span Crimson Peak and Pacific Rim to Suicide Squad, Edge of Tomorrow and The Hobbit. Her work has previously earned an Emmy nomination, a Costume Designers Guild Award and Saturn and Empire award" - (Fashion United UK)

Kate’s body of work speaks for itself. She’s another fantastic story of a career that started at home in Aotearoa and went global,

We’ll pick her brain (not in a Frankenstein way) about her career, her craft, and what it takes to build a whole world out of fabric, dye and attention to detail. Moderated by Robin Laing.

Date: Tuesday 17th November

Time: Drinks from 6pm | Talk 6:30-8pm

Location: Wētā Workshop Space, 129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington

WIFT Members free, non-members $25. Drinks and nibbles provided.

long_description:
If you’re new here, welcome - stoked you found us!

We’re tipsy trails. We’re on a mission to get more people in their 20s outdoors and turn an online community into a seriously epic in-person one.

We walk together along some of New Zealand’s most stunning trails, chatting with new and old mates - usually wrapping things up with a well-earned beverage afterwards.

We’re a club built on the idea that getting outdoors doesn’t have to be super serious or intense - it should be accessible, with a bit of fun. You don’t need fancy gear. You don’t need to be “outdoorsy.” You don’t even need a group to come with - rocking up solo is totally normal here. All paces and abilities are welcome. You just need to show up and enjoy the rest.

So, what do you say? Put down your phone and come outside with us.

⛰️ TRAIL INFO

Trail: Skyline Track, Johnsonville

Length: Out & back (halfway), approx. 12km, 460m elevation gain, around 3 hours

Difficulty: Rated Moderate by AllTrails

🎒 WHAT TO BRING?

Water bottle (make sure it’s full!)

comfy walking shoes,

a warm layer for during and after the hike 🧥,

a waterproof jacket (just in case 🌧️),

trail snacks (interpret this however your heart desires),

hat, sunglasses, and sunscreen (fingers crossed for sunshine ☀️),

a bag to throw everything in (backpack or side bag works perfectly 🎒)

📍 MEETING POINT

Meeting details and timing will be emailed once you’ve registered.

Keep an eye on our Instagram and tipsy trails Facebook messenger group chats for any updates or weather changes.

🍻 POST-HIKE PLANS?

With the trail wrapped up and the afternoon still ahead, we’ll head to a nearby pub for a well-earned beverage and bite to eat!


🚙 NEED / CAN OFFER A LIFT

Carpooling is available for anyone who needs a lift or can offer one. Once you have registered, you can connect with others in the Facebook messenger carpool group chat, share your area, and organise pick-up details directly.

🥾 REGISTRATION

This is a free community event with limited spots. Registration is required.

Got questions? Our DM’s are always open on Instagram @tipsy_____________

id: 2026 Korea Wellington Business Breakfast-2 Harris Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: 2026 Korea Wellington Business Breakfast
venue: 2 Harris Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Mark 10 years since the formal city-to-city partnership between Wellington and its sister city Seoul, with Korean and New Zealand business leaders, officials and organisations over a Korean-inspired breakfast.

Description:

The Embassy of the Republic of Korea, Wellington City Council and the Korea New Zealand Business Council (KNZBC) are pleased to invite you to the 2026 Korea Wellington Business Breakfast.

Seoul is Wellington’s sister city, and this year marks 10 years since the formal city-to-city partnership was established during an official mayoral visit, further strengthening the relationship between our two cities. The breakfast brings together Korean and New Zealand businesses, organisations and officials to explore the opportunities shaping the relationship between our two countries, from trade and investment to primary industries, infrastructure and the creative sector.

Held in Te Akapuanga o Waimānga, the Māori whare within the Wellington City Council building, the morning will open with a karakia and mihimihi. This is followed by remarks from Wellington City Council and the Korean Ambassador, a keynote address from Deer Industry New Zealand, and a panel discussion with business leaders sharing practical experiences of working with Korea, including Q&A.

Guests will enjoy a breakfast with a Korean twist alongside tea and coffee.

This is a great opportunity to connect with others who share an interest in the continued growth of the New Zealand–Korea relationship. We look forward to welcoming you.

Agenda

7:30am — Registration, networking, tea and coffee

7:45am — Mihi and welcome

Karakia and mihimihi, Wellington City Council

7:50am — Opening remarks

Wellington City Council

H.E. Byung-ha Chung, Ambassador of the Republic of Korea to New Zealand

8:00am — Keynote address: New Zealand’s Deer Industry in Korea

Terry Meikle, Market Manager, Deer Industry New Zealand

8:15am — Panel discussion and Q&A: Business Partnership in Practice

David Sheppard, General Manager, Hyundai Rotem

John McKay, Managing Director, POW Studios

Further panellist to be announced

8:45am — Closing remarks

Gareth Coleman, Chair, Korea New Zealand Business Council

8:50am — Breakfast and networking

9:30am — Event ends

name: AoJO November Improvisation Workshops: Beginner
venue: Level 5/39 Webb Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. Whether you're taking your first steps into improvisation or looking to deepen existing skills, these sessions are designed to provide a safe, comfortable, and supportive environment in which to experiment, learn, and grow as a musician.

Beginner

The Beginner workshop is for musicians of all ages who are fairly new to jazz and improvisation and wish to get started on their journey.

This workshop will offer participants an entry point into jazz styles, group listening, and the foundational elements of ensemble playing, with the goal of learning to play and improvise on a jazz standard.

You'll have the opportunity to play alongside a professional rhythm section in a safe, comfortable, and supportive learning environment, where experimentation and curiosity are encouraged.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

Suitable for students, amateurs, and anyone wanting to begin their jazz journey.

"The musicians created such a safe and comfortable learning environment and were genuinely encouraging. There were too many great takeaways and learnings to list, but it inspired me to keep working and experimenting. I'm really looking forward to the follow-up session."

– Helen, workshop participant

name: Women of Pōneke November 2026 Event
venue: 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Women of Pōneke : Together by Design - The Next Chapter

26 November |5pm -7.30pm | Te Ahumairangi Foyer

National Library 70 Molesworth St

Women of Pōneke exists to elevate women in our city, and it starts with connection. We are ambitious about where that can go, and we are here to serve the women who make it what it is.

On Thursday 26 November, we are bringing everyone together for an evening that is Together by Design.

First and foremost, this is a night out: lively, warm and relaxed. Come with a crowd, or come on your own and leave having met someone new. Expect laughter, easy conversation and time to unwind in a welcoming space, the Te Ahumairangi Foyer at the National Library on Molesworth Street in Thorndon.

The food will be amazing and you will leave well nourished. Everybody Eats, the social enterprise that looked after us in September, is providing the platters, and Luna Estate will be pouring the wine. We are paying Everybody Eats the full value of the catering, so every ticket helps a social enterprise thrive and puts our community’s support to work close to home.

The evening also opens a conversation about what comes next. We have some big ideas, and we reckon you will too. Women of Pōneke is working with Kathryn Robinson and Celine Yockney from Verian, who have generously contributed their research and engagement expertise to help us design the event and make sense of what we hear from you.

We will talk it through over a glass of bubbles or juice. We will share a little of our thinking, we want to hear yours, and your answers will shape what we build.

A ticket gets you good food, warm company and a seat at the table for what comes next. All are welcome, so bring a colleague, invite someone whose company you enjoy and come ready to have fun. We cannot wait to see you there.

We know things are busy in the run to the end of the year, so here are four reasons to come:

Nourishing kai and wine: platters from Everybody Eats, with Luna Estate pouring.

Warm company: familiar faces and new ones, in an evening built for connecting and unwinding.

Your ticket makes a difference: the full catering value supports a social enterprise.

A seat at the table: big ideas for what comes next, shaped by you.

So grab your ticket now and share with at least one amazing woman (and/or ally) in your life.

To cover our costs, we are charging for this event. We know that things are tough at the moment for many, so if this is a barrier for you to attend, please contact us and we will do everything to support you to attend. 

Help a woman in need

If you wish to support someone else who may have a financial barrier, please buy one of the "Buy-One, Give-One" tickets, so we can support more of the amazing women of Pōneke to attend.

Get in quick!

Tickets for previous events have sold out fast. For this event we are capped at 250 people attending and we will be updating our social media channels on the progress of the ticket sales, so get your tickets quick.  

Accessibility
The Te Ahumairangi Foyer, National Library is fully accessible. If you are not able to use the steps on Molesworth Street, you will be able to access the venue via the lift off Aitken Street. There will be staff at the door to be able to support and guide you to the venue space.

A bit about us 

Me.We.Pōneke is our signature quarterly event designed to inspire, connect and raise the voices of our wonderful community of Wellington women, and people who identify as women. 

We believe that magic happens when women come together. We’ve seen it. We’ve felt it. And we want to create more of it with regular events that are open, welcoming, supportive and empowering for the women of Wellington.

Come along, bring a friend and join us as we continue to raise the voices of Wellington women and invite you all to be part of Me We Pōneke.

We are so grateful to all of our supporters, especially Steph and the team at Inside Recruitment.

You can join our mailing list from website, thanks to our amazing partner Springload. Check it out here and make sure you sign up to our mailing list: https://www.womenofponeke.org....

We are also on Insta! Follow us here: https://www.instagram.com/wome…

At the same time, insurers are rethinking traditional products to meet the evolving needs of more New Zealanders, regulatory reform and a tough economic climate. That pressure is pushing insurers to rethink how they're built and to find new ways to support customers in sustainable ways.

Join the InsurTech community in Wellington on 12th November to hear how life and health insurers are innovating.

In the lead up to the launch of Acenda Life in New Zealand in 2027, we’ll hear what has been learned by Asteron Life following their exit from Suncorp and acquisition by Resolution Life Australasia with a further ownership structure to being a member of the Nippon Life Group.  The presentation will further focus on learnings from a digital, data and customer experience perspective.

Then a panel of insurance and insurtech leaders will look at the big issues and trends shaping the sector into 2027. They'll cover how AI is being used in practice today, the opportunities Open Data could open up, and what makes partnerships between insurers and insurtechs work. Hear from Asteron Life, Deloitte, Life Direct, Monvia, Partners Life and Simfuni.

Register now to attend this event and connect with insurance and data professionals. Generously supported by Deloitte and Asteron Life.

Time:  5:00PM - 7.00PM

Location: Deloitte's offices, 20 Customhouse Quay.

Well Ahead brings together Dame Susan Devoy and a lineup of experts across health, nutrition, movement and healthy ageing to explore the science and strategy behind:

Energy and recovery

Sleep and stress

Nutrition

Strength and movement

Body composition

Hormonal changes

Perimenopause and menopause

Bone health

Genetics and individual biology

Well Ahead is designed as a connected conversation, not a series of standalone talks.

Each speaker builds on the last, giving you a clearer, more complete picture of your own health rather than a list of disconnected tips.

long_description:
KIM CHURCHILL LIVE IN WELLINGTON!

One man. A guitar, harmonica, percussion and an extraordinary voice. A whole world of sound.

Australian singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Kim Churchill returns to New Zealand for a very special evening of world-class live music at the beautiful Old St Paul's!

From the legendary stages of Glastonbury and the Montreal Jazz Festival to intimate venues around the world, Kim has built an international reputation for his captivating one-man-band performances, incredible guitar playing and heartfelt songwriting.

Blending folk, blues, roots and indie music, Kim creates a remarkable live experience. Intricate fingerpicking, rhythmic guitar percussion, harmonica, foot drums and soaring vocals somehow come together through just one performer.

His much-loved song Window to the Sky went platinum in Australia, and his music has reached millions of listeners around the world.

But it's on stage where Kim Churchill truly comes alive. His shows move from explosive, foot-stomping energy to beautifully intimate moments, with warmth, humour and stories from a lifetime spent travelling the world playing music.

Whether you're already a fan or discovering Kim for the first time, this is a concert not to be missed!

CONCERT DETAILS

📍 Old St Paul's, Wellington

📅 24 February 2027

🚪 Doors open 7:00pm

🎶 Concert starts 7:30pm

✨ Fully seated, intimate listening-room concert

ABOUT KIM CHURCHILL

Raised in the coastal town of Merimbula, Australia, Kim Churchill began his musical journey as a young busker before setting off around the world with a guitar, a surfboard and a remarkable talent for songwriting.

After winning the Byron Bay Bluesfest busking competition, Kim went on to perform at major international festivals, share stages with celebrated musicians and build a devoted global audience.

His distinctive one-man-band style is something that really needs to be seen to be believed. Combining technically brilliant acoustic guitar work with percussion, harmonica and a powerful, expressive voice, Kim creates a sound far bigger than one person should be capable of.

Yet beyond the extraordinary musicianship lies a gifted songwriter whose music reflects a lifelong love of travel, nature, connection and the freedom of the open road.

ABOUT THE VENUE

In the heart of Wellington, Old St Paul's is one of New Zealand's most breathtaking heritage venues, renowned for its magnificent timber architecture, soaring vaulted ceilings and extraordinary atmosphere.

For one night, Nightingale Concerts brings its intimate listening-room experience to this iconic former church, offering audiences the chance to enjoy a remarkable Australian touring artist in one of Wellington's most beautiful and historic settings.

Expect an evening of exceptional music, heartfelt songs, extraordinary guitar playing and the kind of connection that makes live performance so special.

🎟️ TICKETS ARE ON SALE NOW!

From international festival stages to intimate concert halls around the world, Kim Churchill has captivated audiences with his extraordinary live performances.

Don't miss your chance to experience him up close in Wellington. Secure your tickets today!

Write it. Test the AI. Trust your judgement.

Can AI really improve your writing? Or does it sometimes get things wrong?

Join Viet Hub NZ for a FREE, fun and interactive writing workshop where YOU get to challenge AI, spot its mistakes and discover how to become a more confident writer.

🌟 Meet your workshop leader – Kai.

We're excited to have Kai (Anh Khoa Dang), one of Viet Hub NZ's passionate young volunteers, leading this workshop.

At Viet Hub NZ, we believe young people have incredible ideas and deserve opportunities to bring them to life.

Kai has already been supporting learners through our IELTS Writing sessions. Now he's taking the next step – designing and leading his own workshop to help others develop practical writing skills.

Young minds. Bold ideas. The courage to try something new!

Come along, learn something useful and support a young community leader!

This isn't a workshop where you just sit and listen. You'll be writing, experimenting, discussing and putting AI to the test!

Hey → Dear! Turn a casual text message into a professional email. Can you write a better version than AI?

Spot the 8 writing traps! Discover common mistakes in tone, vocabulary and structure.

Choose your writing challenge! Write an email, job application paragraph or short essay.

Let AI mark your words! Ask AI to review your writing and see what it notices.

Human vs AI! Compare AI's feedback with another participant's. Who catches more mistakes?

This workshop is particularly useful for:

School and university students

IELTS and English-language learners

Jobseekers preparing applications

Anyone who wants to write clearer, more professional emails

Curious minds who want to learn how to use AI responsibly

long_description:
Jazz and Beyond for students 19 and under

December 14–17, 2026

Coordinated by Chris Beernink, Dave Wilson, Daniel Hayles, Andrew Faleatua, Lance Philip. Proudly supported by the Tauranga Jazz Society.

Take it to the next level as a player or vocalist at the Jazz and Beyond Workshops! Young musicians from across Aotearoa come together to dive into jazz and connected styles, working closely with some of the country’s leading performers and educators. In a friendly, inclusive environment, you’ll grow your skills, make new musical connections, and learn alongside other students your age from all around the motu.

Here’s what’s in store:

small group ensembles led by professional musicians

developing improvisation skills in supportive settings

an introduction to music production

listening sessions that expand your skills

inclusive jam sessions where all are welcome

ensemble performances at the end of week concert

And more!

If you're 19 or under with at least a year of experience on your instrument or in vocal training, you’re welcome to join. Choose from trumpet, trombone, saxophone, clarinet, flute, bass, piano, guitar, drums, vibraphone, or voice.

The workshops are held at the New Zealand School of Music–Te Kōkī at Te Herenga Waka-Victoria University of Wellington. Follow the Jazz and Beyond Workshops on Instagram or Facebook for the latest updates. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com with any questions.

Schedule

The workshops run 9:00am-4:30pm Monday through Thursday, with evening activities including concerts and our inclusive jam sessions Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday. Students perform in a closing concert on Thursday afternoon.

Accommodation

Students arrange their own accommodation. Often students from outside Wellington stay together in groups with a parent chaperone. Options for housing near Victoria University of Wellington include backpacker hostels and hotels. If you have a group of 15 or more, University Student Housing may be an option. Email jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com if you'd like to pursue this option.

Meals

Lunch for the four days is available for purchase at many convenient locations on campus, or students may bring their own lunch.

Equipment

Provided equipment includes drum kits, guitar and bass amps, pianos/keyboards, microphones and PAs for vocalists.

All brass and wind players should bring their own instruments.

Drummers: you are required to bring your own cymbals, sticks, and hi-hat clutch.

Guitarists and bass players: you are required to bring your own instruments as well as cables (leads).

Preparation

All students with one year of experience on an instrument or in vocal training have the skills required to participate, so no musical preparation is required. On the first day, students will play a very short audition to be placed in an appropriate ensemble. Guidelines for this short audition will be sent to all registered participants in advance of the workshops.

Cost

Early bird price: $325 - register before 19th October

Standard price $350 - on or after 19th October

Registration is open to all until all spots are filled.

We are dedicated to ensuring all students can participate in the workshops without financial constraints. If the cost poses a barrier, please email us at jazzandbeyondworkshops@gmail.com and we will find a solution to facilitate your participation!

long_description:
AJO Jazz Improvisation Workshops

The Aotearoa Jazz Orchestra is pleased to present the next instalment of its jazz improvisation workshop series.

Hosted by cross-genre performer Oscar Lavën, alongside a professional jazz rhythm section, these highly accessible workshops are designed to help musicians build confidence in improvisation through listening, playing, and creative exploration. Particularly suited to musicians from a classical background, the workshops are open to players of all instruments, ages, and musical backgrounds.

Participants in previous workshops praised the supportive atmosphere, practical learning, and encouragement they received while exploring new musical ideas. Whether you're taking your first steps into improvisation or looking to deepen existing skills, these sessions are designed to provide a safe, comfortable, and supportive environment in which to experiment, learn, and grow as a musician.

Beginner

The Beginner workshop is for musicians of all ages who are fairly new to jazz and improvisation and wish to get started on their journey.

This workshop will offer participants an entry point into jazz styles, group listening, and the foundational elements of ensemble playing, with the goal of learning to play and improvise on a jazz standard.

You'll have the opportunity to play alongside a professional rhythm section in a safe, comfortable, and supportive learning environment, where experimentation and curiosity are encouraged.

Workshop places are limited, allowing plenty of opportunity for individual participation, discussion, and playing time with the rhythm section.

Suitable for students, amateurs, and anyone wanting to begin their jazz journey.

"The musicians created such a safe and comfortable learning environment and were genuinely encouraging. There were too many great takeaways and learnings to list, but it inspired me to keep working and experimenting. I'm really looking forward to the follow-up session."

– Helen, workshop participant

Cameron Bennett and Chris Priestley -with special guest Angela Fox- share songs, stories and a slideshow from NZ's distant past. Together, they bring to life the characters and stories of our past - the quirky and macabre - that shaped who we are today.

Chris Priestley is a singer, songwriter & NZ historian. He has recorded eight albums and his musical spans over 40 years. As a hospitality entrepreneur he was co-founder of Real Groovy Records & café/music venues Java Jive, Kerouacs, Atomic and Café One2One in Ponsonby.

id: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington-31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington
venue: 31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40 for waged and $20 for unwaged, fully refundable until one day prior.

id: Bach, Bells & Christmas — Concert by Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington-71 Woburn Road, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Bach, Bells & Christmas — Concert by Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington
venue: 71 Woburn Road, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Celebrate the richness and wonder of Christmas with Cantoris and Festival Singers of Wellington, as they join forces for an evening of music that spans centuries, crosses continents and brings together joyful celebration and quiet reflection.

Conducted by Ingrid Schoenfeld, who directs both, the two choirs will be accompanied by well-known organists Jonathan Berkahn and Heather Easting. Together, they bring a wealth of musical experience to a programme filled with colour, contrast and seasonal spirit.

At the heart of the concert is Cantata V of J.S. Bach’s Christmas Oratorio, opening with the chorus Ehre sei dir, Gott, gesungen. This part of Bach’s great Christmas work follows the journey of the Magi, exploring their search for the newborn Jesus and the image of light shining through darkness. Its combination of exuberant choral writing, storytelling and reflection offers a vivid encounter with the Christmas narrative.

Felix Mendelssohn’s Die deutsche Liturgie brings another dimension to the evening. Its Kyrie, Gloria and Sanctus move from prayerful appeal to praise and adoration, revealing the composer’s gift for expressive melody and beautifully shaped choral textures. These three movements offer moments of warmth, grandeur and stillness.

Music from Aotearoa New Zealand has a special place in this concert. Jonathan Berkahn’s Four Christmas Songs brings together Unto us a Son is given, Meditation – rorate coeli desuper, And art thou come with us to dwell? and How sweet the angels song. The sequence invites listeners to consider Christmas through proclamation, contemplation and a sense of wonder. With Berkahn also appearing as one of the evening’s organists, the concert offers a particularly personal connection between the music and its composer.

Jenny McLeod’s Vulcan and Indigo II, from her Sun Festival Carols, add further New Zealand colour.

Philip Stopford’s Lully, Lulla, Lullay provides a tender, haunting contrast. Drawing on the Coventry Carol text, it captures both the intimacy of a lullaby and the poignancy beneath the Christmas story. John Gardner’s Tomorrow shall be my dancing day brings buoyant rhythm and infectious vitality, while Mykola Leontovich’s Carol of the Bells sparkles with its familiar repeating motif and gathering excitement.

From Bach’s joyful praise to the delicacy of a lullaby, this programme offers much to discover and enjoy.

St James’ Anglican Church in Lower Hutt provides a welcoming setting, with comfortable seating and a crisp acoustic in which to savour the combined voices and accompaniment.

Make time in the busy December season for an evening of shared listening, musical discovery and festive warmth. Join Festival Singers of Wellington, Cantoris, Ingrid Schoenfeld, Jonathan Berkahn and Heather Easting for Bach, Bells and Christmas: a celebration of the season through the expressive power of choral music.

[Children 18 years and under enter free when accompanied by a paying adult.]

venue: 13 Vennell Street, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
$25

Limited door sales for $30

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1-hour gong bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy, particularly gong baths, in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the gongs, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1-hour gong bath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY

Disclaimer
Gong baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first.

About Me
Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 30+ years musical experience. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

Whether you’re a seasoned adventurer or you’ve never rolled a die in your life, this two-hour, beginner-friendly D&D experience at Titahi Bay’s own Beer Engine is for you.

S-ence returns to the Cuba St Tavern Courtyard with a special concept night to warm your winter blues.

Essential Selections feat
Matt Drake | Jen Kyle | Coda

After playing alongside each other at Arkadien last year, this powerhouse-trio hatched the idea of playing a concept night together where they each would go a bit more free-range and play sets and tracks that riff off each other. Not quite a B2B session but definitely as much fun.

Jen Kyle's cult following continues to grow - synonymous for her DJ sets where she journeys through everything from techno to disco, punk to funk, soul to hip hop, new wave and beyond.

Expect an Essential Selection spanned early and lates sets from all three selectors with lots of fun on and off the decks.

Early doors, early night.

id: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science-93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science
venue: 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS is a documentary that dives into the extraordinary true story of the Unarius Academy of Science, an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school founded in El Cajon in the 1970s. Led by the dazzlingly outlandish Ruth E. Norman—revered as "Archangel Uriel"—Unarius evolved into a wildly inventive public-access television phenomenon. The group produced films that appeared to be elaborately campy space epics yet were, at their core, sincere therapeutic works. 

From The Source Family director Jodi Wille comes another mind-expanding voyage into the wild frontiers of American belief, bringing her singular blend of empathy, humor, and emotional insight to one of the country's most fascinating outsider communities. Produced by Caryn Capotosto (Won’t You Be My Neighbor) and Jodi Wille. Executive producers include Elijah Wood, Moby, and Oscar-winning filmmakers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.

Please join us for the Wellington screening of WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS - brought to you by Erika Grant and Night Church Cinema. This is a dress up event - come dressed in your favorite UFO/Cult fit. There will be prizes for best dressed, and DJ's Oona Verse and Martyn Pepperell plus others will guide us into the wild starry night with space cult inspired dance tracks.

The bar and restaurant will be open for dinner and drinks. This is a one off event, not to be missed!!

“Wild and Very Trippy” - Jodi Wille

“If I didn’t know Jodi Wille’s film, Welcome Space Brothers, was a documentary, I’d swear it was a WTF, insane, sci-fi tale of weirdness. The story of Ruth is fascinating…..” - Alan NG, Film Threat 

“It’s a vision of healing, acceptance, peace, cooperation, and hope, expressed through an outpouring of unbridled creative energy. If that spells crazy, beam me up!” — Doug Harvey, Artillery

venue: 46a Victoria Street, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
long_description:
Originally from the wilds of the south west of the UK, Phil Lively-Masters is an experienced, dynamic and well travelled singer songwriter, who specialises in writing the sort of Sun Kissed West Coast Laurel Canyon Americana and Roots Rock that made Neil Young, Stephen Stills, the Byrds and 'Wildflowers' era Tom Petty famous. With a powerful, honey soaked voice that has won praise and support slots from the likes of legendary American country rock pioneers The Jayhawks, Lemonheads frontman Evan Dando, original outlaw cosmic cowboy Steve Young (writer of Seven Bridges Road), Neil Halstead (Slowdive, Mojave 3) and received critical praise for acoustic slots at festivals such as Glastonbury and Maverick in the UK. 

Now based in Napier, Hawke's Bay, Phil has 20 years worth of road worn original songs to pull on, covering all the Roots/ Americana elements, with a skilful blend of Country, Rock, Blues and Folk. Having recently been inspired by a sonmgwriting stint in East Nashville, Phil came back to NZ and teamed up with local Lead guitar Telecaster Master Neil Matcheson as a new Americana duo 'The Lone Prairie Brothers', they are currently in the process of short listing songs for a new self titled debut album and racking up live gigs and great reviews in 2026, weaving Phil's trusty Guild 12 and 6 string guitars with Neil's versatile and exciting Telecaster licks; airing brand new songs and including some choice tracks from Phil's previous critically acclaimed UK band CANYON RYDE, (and their album 'Free To Be'), ready to weave a sun kissed, melodic americana spell on any listener.

Reviews for the Canyon Ryde album...

UNCUT MAGAZINE: ‘A prime platter...perfect for those attuned to the soft driftwood sounds of Buffalo Springfield and Gram Parsons'

MOJO MAGAZINE: ‘An excellent and very mature sounding debut in ‘Free to Be’. Another fine example of a talented ‘under the radar’ outfit producing American inspired music as good as, if not better, than a lot of Americans on the same trip. Highly Recommended!’

Sony/Universal Music Historian Richard Havers: ‘Big Names in The Making’…The MAVERICK AMERICANA FESTIVAL... the opening act on the main stage was the intriguingly named Canyon Ryde, featuring the exquisite songs of Phil Lively-Masters. Imagine you’ve been stranded on a California hill farm circa 1969 and you get the vibe. Their music is just so damned catchy!’

MAVERICK MAGAZINE: ‘CANYON RYDE is the vehicle for singer-songwriter Phil Lively-Masters and his superb songs that are evocative of America’s West Coast countryish pop-rock of the late 1960s and early 1970s… with acclaimed players such as singer songwriter Peter Bruntnell and Gary Louris… It is a gorgeous listening experience, especially on the captivating ‘Marine Drive’.

AMERICANA UK: ‘’Subtle and dreamy country boasting a host of Americana luminaries... ‘Free to Be’ is a great country record that is subtle in its approach, gentle in its intentions"

id: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington-31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: One Day Secular Meditation Retreat in Wellington
venue: 31 Lawson Place, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
We know from ancient wisdom and modern psychology that meditation brings many benefits for our mental and physical wellbeing. It can reduce worry and pain, and improve calmness, focus, sleep, relationships and life satisfaction. The more time we spend meditating, and the more skilled we become, the greater the benefits.

So take a restorative break from your daily life, meet other meditators, and strengthen your practice at this small-group retreat. Everyone is welcome, whatever their level of meditation experience or preferred style. The retreat is beginner-friendly, and our approach is secular (meaning non-religious) which makes room for diverse beliefs.

The programme

We will begin with introductions, followed by a guided meditation that covers the core skills of both sitting and walking meditation. For the rest of the day, the meditation will be unguided apart from occasional bells to announce breaks, and to remind you to alternate between sitting and walking (if that's what you choose to do).

To help quieten the mind, many participants prefer not to talk again until the discussion circle at the end of the retreat. However some people like to chat with others during the breaks, and there is space allocated for this. The retreat leaders are always available for quiet conversations if you need support with your practice.

The venue

The Innermost Gardens hall is nestled between the central city suburb of Mount Victoria and the green town belt. This provides a peaceful nature-rich setting for the retreat, surrounded by community gardens to enjoy during the breaks or walking meditation.

There will be hot drinks and snacks available throughout the day. For lunch the participants bring a plate of vegetarian food to share. The venue has a full kitchen including cutlery, plates, bowls, fridge, stove, and a microwave.

The leaders

Bryan Royds is an adult educator and registered counsellor with a passion for wellbeing science and leadership development. He has been meditating and teaching meditation skills in groups for many years, including the well-researched methods of Mindfulness Based Stress Reduction (MBSR).

Sarah Jane Barnett is a writer and creative writing teacher at Massey University. She has been a Buddhist for ten years, practicing mostly Vipassana meditation. She also co-facilitates a meditation group for people who practice Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (an evidence-based modern psychotherapy and wellbeing method).

The registration fee is only $40 for waged and $20 for unwaged, fully refundable until one day prior.

long_description:
KIM CHURCHILL LIVE IN WELLINGTON!

One man. A guitar, harmonica, percussion and an extraordinary voice. A whole world of sound.

Australian singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Kim Churchill returns to New Zealand for a very special evening of world-class live music at the beautiful Old St Paul's!

From the legendary stages of Glastonbury and the Montreal Jazz Festival to intimate venues around the world, Kim has built an international reputation for his captivating one-man-band performances, incredible guitar playing and heartfelt songwriting.

Blending folk, blues, roots and indie music, Kim creates a remarkable live experience. Intricate fingerpicking, rhythmic guitar percussion, harmonica, foot drums and soaring vocals somehow come together through just one performer.

His much-loved song Window to the Sky went platinum in Australia, and his music has reached millions of listeners around the world.

But it's on stage where Kim Churchill truly comes alive. His shows move from explosive, foot-stomping energy to beautifully intimate moments, with warmth, humour and stories from a lifetime spent travelling the world playing music.

Whether you're already a fan or discovering Kim for the first time, this is a concert not to be missed!

CONCERT DETAILS

📍 Old St Paul's, Wellington

📅 24 February 2027

🚪 Doors open 7:00pm

🎶 Concert starts 7:30pm

✨ Fully seated, intimate listening-room concert

ABOUT KIM CHURCHILL

Raised in the coastal town of Merimbula, Australia, Kim Churchill began his musical journey as a young busker before setting off around the world with a guitar, a surfboard and a remarkable talent for songwriting.

After winning the Byron Bay Bluesfest busking competition, Kim went on to perform at major international festivals, share stages with celebrated musicians and build a devoted global audience.

His distinctive one-man-band style is something that really needs to be seen to be believed. Combining technically brilliant acoustic guitar work with percussion, harmonica and a powerful, expressive voice, Kim creates a sound far bigger than one person should be capable of.

Yet beyond the extraordinary musicianship lies a gifted songwriter whose music reflects a lifelong love of travel, nature, connection and the freedom of the open road.

ABOUT THE VENUE

In the heart of Wellington, Old St Paul's is one of New Zealand's most breathtaking heritage venues, renowned for its magnificent timber architecture, soaring vaulted ceilings and extraordinary atmosphere.

For one night, Nightingale Concerts brings its intimate listening-room experience to this iconic former church, offering audiences the chance to enjoy a remarkable Australian touring artist in one of Wellington's most beautiful and historic settings.

Expect an evening of exceptional music, heartfelt songs, extraordinary guitar playing and the kind of connection that makes live performance so special.

🎟️ TICKETS ARE ON SALE NOW!

From international festival stages to intimate concert halls around the world, Kim Churchill has captivated audiences with his extraordinary live performances.

Don't miss your chance to experience him up close in Wellington. Secure your tickets today!

venue: 67 Futuna Close, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
‘TONES of SILENCE’ – FUTUNA CHAPEL in BLACK & WHITE - EXHIBITION 2026

The ‘Tones of Silence’ -explored through B & W photography taken with vintage camera and lenses to give another way of viewing and experiencing the Chapel. This exhibition will explore the tones, textures, composition and forms of the Chapel in black and white with many shades of grey.

"Generally, the older the equipment, the greater the personal input of the photographer is required and therefore the greater the commitment and individuality. Often, you can look at a 19th-century photograph and tell who the photographer is. You certainly can't do that today. It isn't only the camera and lens, but also the type of film (or in those days, glass plate), the developer used and how the print is made onto particular types of paper. Each gives a distinct interpretation".

John Grace - email - 18/06/25

The Trust looks forward to welcoming architects, designers, graduates, students and interested members of the public to attend this event and support the Trust in its work.

The Futuna Trust is a charitable organisation and all koha received from the exhibition events will go towards the ongoing care, maintenance and operation of Futuna Chapel and also to support various initiatives undertaken by the Trust.  Please register

REGISTRATION IS PREFERRED TO ATTEND THIS EVENT. Note that the sunday exhibition hours are 11:00am to 2:00pm. This allows for the public talks that commence at 2:00pm.

long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

WHAT THE PRESS IS SAYING ABOUT SHAUN KIRK

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

"My faith in this generation’s music has been restored.” - Dearhead Press

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

id: Ocean Film Festival World Tour 2027 - Wellington Thurs 11 Mar 6pm-10 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix

venue: 10 Kent Terrace, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Immerse yourself in a breathtaking 3-hour cinematic journey into the world’s most spectacular marine environments. The Ocean Film Festival World Tour brings together an extraordinary collection of short films celebrating the beauty, power and wonder of our oceans.

From crystal-clear tropical reefs and wild coastlines to towering waves and the depths of the open ocean, these beautifully crafted films showcase the ocean from every perspective. Meet the passionate divers, fearless surfers, dedicated ocean advocates, ocean explorers and marine scientists whose lives are shaped by their connection to the sea.

Featuring spectacular underwater cinematography, heart-stopping ocean adventures and intimate stories of the people who dedicate their lives to exploring and protecting our oceans, every film offers a fresh perspective on the world beneath the waves.

Along the way, encounter remarkable marine creatures, discover remote underwater environments and experience the thrill of ocean adventure through the eyes of those who know it best.

The Ocean Film Festival World Tour is a celebration of our oceans in all their beauty, diversity and power. Inspiring, entertaining and thought-provoking, it’s an unforgettable experience that will leave you with a deeper appreciation for the incredible marine environments that connect us all.

Find out more at https://oceanfilmfestivalworldtour.com/tickets-new-zealand/

 

The Ocean Film Festival is exempt from Classification, but all swearing has been beeped out.

Recommended age 10+

name: FLINT Wellington: Get to Know a CxO
venue: level 6/44 Bowen Street, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.

id: Te Whiri Whītau 2026: Fibre Futures - Connections, Reflections and Possibilities-Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Te Whiri Whītau 2026: Fibre Futures - Connections, Reflections and Possibilities
venue: Wallace Street, Mount Cook, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Come and join Te Whiri Whītau as we celebrate a year of learning, making, connecting and dreaming together.

We warmly invite you to join in conversation, connection and celebration as we reflect on the year that has been and share our aspirations for the future. This gathering is an opportunity to learn more about the work of Te Whiri Whītau, hear about current and emerging research, meet our researchers and collaborators, and explore opportunities for collaboration, partnership, creative practice and research.

Over the course of the event, we'll share research highlights, introduce our new visual identity, and open conversations about the role that fibres, textiles and materials can play in creating thriving communities, cultures, environments and economies.

Whether you are a researcher, practitioner, student, industry partner, community organisation or supporter of our work, we would love you to join us as we strengthen connections, celebrate achievements, and look ahead to what's possible together.

Light refreshments will be served.

Connect in person with Aotearoa New Zealand’s EdTech community.

Hosted by EdTechNZ Member  Alsu Sworder from Litmaps, this is an informal event that could formally change the trajectory of your life.

Using citation networks and visual maps, Litmaps makes it easier to discover important research, identify gaps and organise literature. Used by researchers in more than 150 countries, Litmaps is proud to be an EdTechNZ member and supporter of the New Zealand EdTech community.

id: Shaun Kirk - Live @ Undercurrent, Wellington, NZ-118 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Shaun Kirk - Live @ Undercurrent, Wellington, NZ
venue: 118 Tory Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognised for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

WHAT THE PRESS IS SAYING ABOUT SHAUN KIRK

“It’s rare to see someone bring down the house as an opener, but Australia’s Shaun Kirk did exactly that. He connected with the crowd immediately” – Soundcheck Entertainment, Canada

“One of the most explosive acts Australia has to offer” – Mixdown Magazine, Australia

"My faith in this generation’s music has been restored.” - Dearhead Press

“Simply astounding." - Forte Magazine, Australia

Special guest: Joe Cole

long_description:
For the first time in 10 years - Mark Moroney & David Shanhun are reuniting for a series of intimate shows across New Zealand in 2026. This special tour brings their signature blend of world-class guitar playing, heartfelt songwriting, rich harmonies, and light-hearted banter back to audiences around the country. Expect an evening of unforgettable music, plenty of laughs, and the kind of connection that only comes from two great friends & musicians sharing the stage.

This is your chance to see these two acclaimed guitarists and singer-songwriters LIVE in your town!

💫 Intimate Setting

Don’t miss your chance to experience these two exquisite musicians, live and up close.

MARK MORONEY

“A mix of huskiness and honey, Peregian singer, songwriter and acoustic guitarist Mark Moroney’s voice acts like a balm.” Frances Frangenheim, Salt Magazine.

Singer song writer and guitarist Mark Moroney radiates emotion, authenticity and soul.  His style and sound are distilled from a musical melting pot of folk, blues, roots, soul, jazz and pop. 

A favourite at festivals including Woodford Folk Festival (AU), The Mosaic Music Festival (Singapore), & The Bay Of Islands Jazz & Blues Festival (NZ), experiencing Mark live is an unmissable highlight of any show.

DAVID SHANHUN

"Once in a while you see an artist who is out of the ordinary." - The Shirley Ryder Show

David Shanhun has opened for Rock legends Foreigner, & Heart, and has performed in NZ, Japan, Australia, and the UK. His exquisite guitar work shines under his superb storytelling and songwriting. He's performed with Grammy Award winner Bryan White, and is known for his engaging live shows and heartfelt tunes.

name: Deep Listening Sound Bath at Erskine Chapel
venue: 31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington 6023, New Zealand
long_description:
A Deep Listening Soundbath inside the sublime acoustics of Erskine Chapel

$45

Limited door sales for $50

Please bring a yoga mat, pillow, eye mask and blanket - or whatever it is you need to feel most warm and comfortable. Dress comfortably.

Discover the transformative effects of sound therapy with this 1.5hr-hour sound bath experience.

During this session, participants will be surrounded by the resonant vibrations of gongs and taonga pūoro, carefully designed to induce deep states of relaxation and calm. As you settle into the experience, allow the soothing tones to wash over you, releasing tension and promoting a sense of inner peace.

Scientific studies have highlighted the benefits of sound therapy in reducing stress and promoting overall well-being. The rhythmic patterns and overtones of the gongs and other instruments can help entrain brainwaves, leading to a meditative state and improved mental clarity.

Beyond the immediate effects, many participants report experiencing lasting benefits such as improved sleep, reduced anxiety, and enhanced mood following a gong bath session. By immersing yourself in the healing vibrations of the sounds, you can tap into a deeper sense of relaxation and rejuvenation.

Whether you're looking to unwind after a long day or explore new avenues of self-care, this 1.5hr-hour soundbath offers a unique opportunity to reconnect with yourself and find balance amidst the hustle and bustle of daily life. There will be cups of tea available afterwards to help us integrate and ground.

*THIS EVENT IS RESTRICTED TO 40 PEOPLE ONLY**

Disclaimer
Sound baths are safe and supportive for most people. However, please consult your doctor or mental health professional before attending if you:-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)If you have recent injuries, surgeries, or other health concerns, let me know so we can make sure you’re comfortable.

Everyone responds differently to sound. If at any point during the session you feel overwhelmed or uncomfortable, you are welcome to sit up, move gently, or step outside. Your wellbeing always comes first

About Us

Briar Prastiti

Greek–New Zealand composer and vocalist Briar Prastiti is known for her diverse musical practice, spanning contemporary orchestral and chamber music, film, theatre, songwriting, and electronic production. Her most recent compositional project was an epic work for massed choir, solo voice, and taonga pūoro, commissioned for the opening ceremony of Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, Wellington Central Library. In this work, Briar performed as solo vocalist alongside Alistair Fraser on taonga pūoro. 

Alistair Fraser

Alistair is a practitioner of ngā taonga pūoro. He has performed, composed, and collaborated with many of Aotearoa's finest artists, across genres of music and alongside various artistic disciplines since 1999. He worked as a maker, researcher and performer of ngā taonga pūoro nationally and internationally for the past 26 years. He has toured as a soloist with the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra, worked recently with Good Company Arts, Shayne Carter with the Zealand Dance Company for their work Home, Land and Sea, and also for David Long and Stephen Gallagher's score for the Emmy Award winning TV series Secrets at Red Rocks.

Erika Grant

Erika is a musician and astrologer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. She has 35+ years musical experience, in bands, orchestras and various ensembles. She has created music for film, parades and overnight soundbaths. Erika has an interest in the healing properties of sound for mental and physical wellbeing, which she currently explores through her gong bathing practice

long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.

venue: Club K, Kelburn, Te Whanganui-a-Tara 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.

Hailing from Italy and now rooted in Wellington’s vibrant scene, Not My Sister quickly burst onto Aotearoa’s dance floors and has been on a rapid rise ever since. Ryan C is a house and techno DJ based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara (Wellington), NZ.
He spent his formative years travelling solo around the desolate Southern African coast, the stars his blanket and the ocean his teacher.
After being missing for 14 years, he was ‘liberated’ by the Red Cross in Northern Africa ‘working’ on an Ethiopian pirate ship in the Gulf of Aden.
He was in desperate need of revitalisation, so was moved to their base deep in the Amazon basin, in Peru, near the border of Brazil, where he was healed by Amazonian Shamans using an ancient technique.

id: Timothy Blackman 'Between the Islands' Album Release Tour - Wellington-93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Timothy Blackman 'Between the Islands' Album Release Tour - Wellington
venue: 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
Home Alone Music is proud to announce the Aotearoa and Australian tour in celebration of Timothy Blackman's new album 'Between the Islands' (HAM050) in January/February 2027.  

In Aotearoa, there will be full band shows in Wellington and Palmerston North. 

For the full band shows, Timothy's backing band will consist of Tessa Dillion on bass/backing vocals (Mystery Waitress and Tessa de Lyon) and Olivia Campion on drums (Mystery Waitress and Yumi Zouma).

Between the Islands was recorded with a live studio band consisting of Blackman, Tessa Dillon (Mystery Waitress), and Hikurangi Schaverien-Kaa (French for Rabbits, Dateline). Lee Prebble recorded and mixed their performances at The Surgery Recording Studio in Omāroro, Newtown, Wellington over three days in May 2025. Additional overdubs were performed and recorded by Blackman’s longtime collaborator Brooke Singer (French for Rabbits) at her home in Wellington. The album was mastered by Carl Saff in Chicago, Illinois.  Album artwork by Alex Thornton.  


----

Timothy Blackman is a Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington based singer-songwriter, recording artist and founder of independent Aotearoa New Zealand record label Home Alone.

Since his first EP in 2006, Blackman has released a string of acclaimed records such as Modern Sprawl, I've Never Lived, Everyone Needs Something to Hold On To and Brightest Days. Blackman grew up in the Wellington region, began playing violin at five and guitar at ten, and was performing in bands around the Lower Hutt/Wellington area as a teenager. 

His music has since taken him from the bedrooms and small venues of Aotearoa to stages across Europe, the UK, United States and Australia, where he has performed alongside artists including The Mountain Goats and Scout Niblett. His music sits in an intimate space, flitting somewhere between the introspective songwriting of Bill Callahan and Bonnie Prince Billy, and the DIY spirit of New Zealand icon Chris Knox. His songs are personal and unvarnished: thoughtful, melancholic and often quietly funny, with a fascination for place, memory, displacement and the strange details of everyday life.

name: tipsy trails #41 Wellington

long_description:
If you’re new here, welcome - stoked you found us!

We’re tipsy trails. We’re on a mission to get more people in their 20s outdoors and turn an online community into a seriously epic in-person one.

We walk together along some of New Zealand’s most stunning trails, chatting with new and old mates - usually wrapping things up with a well-earned beverage afterwards.

We’re a club built on the idea that getting outdoors doesn’t have to be super serious or intense - it should be accessible, with a bit of fun. You don’t need fancy gear. You don’t need to be “outdoorsy.” You don’t even need a group to come with - rocking up solo is totally normal here. All paces and abilities are welcome. You just need to show up and enjoy the rest.

So, what do you say? Put down your phone and come outside with us.

⛰️ TRAIL INFO

Trail: Skyline Track, Johnsonville

Length: Out & back (halfway), approx. 12km, 460m elevation gain, around 3 hours

Difficulty: Rated Moderate by AllTrails

🎒 WHAT TO BRING?

Water bottle (make sure it’s full!)

comfy walking shoes,

a warm layer for during and after the hike 🧥,

a waterproof jacket (just in case 🌧️),

trail snacks (interpret this however your heart desires),

hat, sunglasses, and sunscreen (fingers crossed for sunshine ☀️),

a bag to throw everything in (backpack or side bag works perfectly 🎒)

📍 MEETING POINT

Meeting details and timing will be emailed once you’ve registered.

Keep an eye on our Instagram and tipsy trails Facebook messenger group chats for any updates or weather changes.

🍻 POST-HIKE PLANS?

With the trail wrapped up and the afternoon still ahead, we’ll head to a nearby pub for a well-earned beverage and bite to eat!


🚙 NEED / CAN OFFER A LIFT

Carpooling is available for anyone who needs a lift or can offer one. Once you have registered, you can connect with others in the Facebook messenger carpool group chat, share your area, and organise pick-up details directly.

🥾 REGISTRATION

This is a free community event with limited spots. Registration is required.

Got questions? Our DM’s are always open on Instagram @tipsy_____________

long_description:
Free Women’s Self-Defence Course: Building Awareness Ahead of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence

Empower yourself with practical skills, confidence, and awareness at this free women’s self-defence session, hosted by the National Council of Women of New Zealand (NCWNZ) Wellington Branch in the lead-up to the international 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign (25 November - 10 December).

Delivered in partnership with Wellington Hapkido Academy, this 90-minute workshop offers a supportive space to learn practical personal safety strategies, build confidence, and raise awareness of gender-based violence prevention.

Event Details

Date: Saturday 21 November 2026

Time: 11:00am – 12:30pm

Cost: FREE!!!

Location: Court 3, Club K, 65 Salamanca Road, Kelburn, Wellington

Parking: Available at 65 Salamanca Road, with additional lower-level parking accessible from within the car park.

What You’ll Learn

Awareness and Prevention

- Body language

- Situational awareness

- Risk reduction strategies

Practical Self-Defence Techniques

- Basic strikes

- Escape techniques

- Using everyday objects for self-defence

Scenario Practice

- Practising responses to simulated high-stress situations

What to Bring and Wear

Clothing: Comfortable clothes you can move in

Footwear: Bare feet, as training takes place on mats

Water: Please bring a water bottle

Emergency contact (optional): You may provide a contact name and phone number for use only in the event of a medical emergency. These details will be kept confidential and destroyed afterwards.

Registration and Donations

This session is completely free, and women are warmly encouraged to attend. Bring a friend, learn practical skills, and build your confidence in a supportive environment. Places are limited, so register early to secure your spot!

Optional donations to the NCWNZ Wellington Branch can be made when booking your ticket. Every contribution supports our ongoing advocacy for gender equality, safety, and community wellbeing in Wellington.

Join us for a practical, empowering session ahead of the 16 Days of Activism, helping build confidence and promote awareness of the importance of preventing gender-based violence.

Can no longer attend? If you register but become unwell or are unable to make it, please email wellington@ncwnz.org.nz as soon as possible so someone else can take your place.
