long_description:
Restoring what was wounded. 

Recovering what was lost. 

Becoming who God created us to be.

 

Do you at times struggle to fully embrace your identity as a son or daughter of God? Do you feel like you know who you are in Christ, but struggle to walk in it completely?

Then this event is for you!

 

Join us for a powerful journey of healing, hope, restoration, and discovery of your identity as a son or daughter of God led by Sandra Sellmer-Kersten.

Through biblical teaching, prayer ministry, and compassionate support, you’ll be invited to encounter Jesus in the places where you’ve experienced pain and discover His invitation to healing and wholeness.

Whether you are personally seeking healing or want to gain some tools to help others walk in and embrace their identity in Christ, this event offers practical insights, spiritual encouragement, and opportunities for prayer and ministry.

 

Sessions include:

The Heart of a King: Restoring what has been wounded and broken.

The Remembering: Remembering who God says we are—and learning to live from that truth.

The Voices: Recovering what shame, fear, pain, and rejection have silenced.

The Forge: Reawakening the unique “song” God has sung over each of us from the beginning.

The Roots: Rediscovering what we were created for—and stepping into what God has entrusted to us with His power and authority. 

 

What to Expect:

Biblical teaching on trauma and healing

Opportunities to receive prayer

A safe, compassionate, and supportive environment

Encouragement, hope, and practical tools for restoration

Included in your ticket:

Morning and afternoon tea will be provided, but please bring your own lunch

A comprehensive manual, usually sold separately for $25

About Sandra:
Sandra Sellmer-Kersten is the founder of House of Nacham Ministries, New Zealand, which she leads alongside her husband, Peter. She previously served for nine years with Elijah House Ministries USA, where she worked as a prayer minister and teacher under the leadership of John and Paula Sandford. Since moving to New Zealand, Sandra began working alongside Elijah House New Zealand, where she facilitates schools, teaches lessons, and has served as a Small Group Leader for 14 years.

Sandra has a deep passion for seeing people encounter the healing love and transforming power of Jesus Christ. Through teaching, prayer ministry, mentoring, and training, she helps people understand the impact of trauma and woundedness, and to find healing, rediscover their God-given identity, and step more fully into who God created them to be.

Her teaching combines biblical truth, practical understanding, personal experience, and more than two decades of ministry experience, with an emphasis on creating a safe and compassionate space for people to honour their stories and encounter Jesus.

This event is not suitable for those under 16.

name: Greccio the Song, a sacred musical inspired by the life of St Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio

long_description:
Greccio: The Song
A sacred musical inspired by the life of Saint Francis of Assisi and the first Nativity at Greccio.
Saturday, 5 December 2026
Matinee: 2:00 PM
Evening Performance: 7:30 PM
Venue: Allan Gibbs Centre, Wellington College, 15 Dufferin StreetMount Victoria, Wellington.

Step into the story of Saint Francis of Assisi, whose longing to contemplate the humility and wonder of Christ’s birth led to the first living Nativity at Greccio in 1223. Greccio: The Song is a community faith-and-arts production bringing together live music, choir, drama, movement, and sacred storytelling in a celebration of faith, family, peace, and renewal. At the heart of the musical is Francis’ desire to make the mystery of Christmas visible and tangible: “We wish to see the Child as He was in Bethlehem.” — St Francis of Assisi.

Through music and dramatic scenes, the production follows Francis’ journey of conversion, simplicity, service, and love of Christ, culminating in the Christmas night at Greccio. The musical features music by Douglas Mews, Dr Robert Loretz, and Franciscan friars from the Philippines, with Artistic/Creative Direction by Dave Cecilio and Musical Direction by Cesar Capistrano.

Presented by Vineyard House — A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family, Greccio: The Song is also part of a special year of commemoration, marking the Jubilee Year of Saint Francis of Assisi (1226–2026) and recognising 60 years of diplomatic relations between New Zealand and the Philippines.

About the production

Greccio: The Song has been created as a community faith and arts initiative, bringing together volunteer actors, musicians, singers, dancers and supporters from across Wellington. It is an invitation to encounter Christmas through the eyes of Saint Francis — not simply as a familiar story, but as a living mystery of humility, joy, peace and love.

Come and let your hearts be renewed.

Presented by: Vineyard House, A Cultural Ministry of the Centre for Marriage and Family

Website: www.marriageandfamily.org.nz⁠

id: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science-93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Welcome Space Brothers - The Extraordinary True Story of the Unarius Academy of Science
venue: 93 Mornington Road, Brooklyn, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
long_description:
WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS is a documentary that dives into the extraordinary true story of the Unarius Academy of Science, an extraterrestrial-channeling spiritual school founded in El Cajon in the 1970s. Led by the dazzlingly outlandish Ruth E. Norman—revered as "Archangel Uriel"—Unarius evolved into a wildly inventive public-access television phenomenon. The group produced films that appeared to be elaborately campy space epics yet were, at their core, sincere therapeutic works. 

From The Source Family director Jodi Wille comes another mind-expanding voyage into the wild frontiers of American belief, bringing her singular blend of empathy, humor, and emotional insight to one of the country's most fascinating outsider communities. Produced by Caryn Capotosto (Won’t You Be My Neighbor) and Jodi Wille. Executive producers include Elijah Wood, Moby, and Oscar-winning filmmakers Phil Lord and Christopher Miller.

Please join us for the Wellington screening of WELCOME SPACE BROTHERS - brought to you by Erika Grant and Night Church Cinema. This is a dress up event - come dressed in your favorite UFO/Cult fit. There will be prizes for best dressed, and DJ's Oona Verse and Martyn Pepperell plus others will guide us into the wild starry night with space cult inspired dance tracks.

The bar and restaurant will be open for dinner and drinks. This is a one off event, not to be missed!!

“Wild and Very Trippy” - Jodi Wille

“If I didn’t know Jodi Wille’s film, Welcome Space Brothers, was a documentary, I’d swear it was a WTF, insane, sci-fi tale of weirdness. The story of Ruth is fascinating…..” - Alan NG, Film Threat 

“It’s a vision of healing, acceptance, peace, cooperation, and hope, expressed through an outpouring of unbridled creative energy. If that spells crazy, beam me up!” — Doug Harvey, Artillery

id: MATRESCENCE Development Showing-12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, Nueva Zelanda-Humanitix
name: MATRESCENCE Development Showing
venue: 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, Nueva Zelanda
long_description:
MATRESCENCE

A development showing at Hannah Playhouse

A solo show about the collision of early motherhood, migration and art making.

A mother tries to care for her baby. An artist tries to make a show.

MATRESCENCE follows Ella (“she” in Spanish), a migrant theatremaker and new mother trying to remain creatively alive while navigating the demands, exhaustion and disorientation of early motherhood.

Part testimonial, part creative crisis and part documentary, MATRESCENCE is an anti-biography that moves between Ella’s intimate experience of postpartum life and her attempt to make theatre from inside it. She reaches out to other migrant mothers and theatremakers, searching for answers about care, identity, creativity and belonging. But the more stories she gathers, the less this seems to be a story about one woman.

Join us for a special development showing of MATRESCENCE at Hannah Playhouse, a glimpse into the making of this new documentary theatre work. This is an opportunity to experience the work in progress and be part of its creative journey.

Following the showing, we invite you to stay for an informal Q&A - audience conversation. We would love to hear your thoughts, reflections and responses to the work, while opening up a wider conversation about postpartum, care work, and the complexities of motherhood, particularly when home, family and support networks are far away.

The work is informed by research into matrescence, migration and caregiving, interviews, as well as anonymous testimonies from migrant mothers living in Aotearoa.

Please note: This is a work in development showing, not a finished production. Your presence, thoughts and feedback are warmly welcomed and will contribute to the ongoing development of MATRESCENCE.

CREATIVE TEAM

Created and performed by Romina Meneses

Directed by Mel Dodge

Production Managment: Jessie Rochford-Barber

Lights and AV design: Janis Cheng

Sound Design: Alex Quinn

Set and Costume Design: Miho Aragane

Photo by Charlie Jewell

MATRESCENCE is a new documentary theatre work, set to premiere at BATS Theatre as part of NZ Fringe 2027.

name: 'TONES OF SILENCE' - FUTUNA CHAPEL IN B&W - EXHIBITION 2026
venue: 67 Futuna Close, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
long_description:
‘TONES of SILENCE’ – FUTUNA CHAPEL in BLACK & WHITE - EXHIBITION 2026

The ‘Tones of Silence’ -explored through B & W photography taken with vintage camera and lenses to give another way of viewing and experiencing the Chapel. This exhibition will explore the tones, textures, composition and forms of the Chapel in black and white with many shades of grey.

"Generally, the older the equipment, the greater the personal input of the photographer is required and therefore the greater the commitment and individuality. Often, you can look at a 19th-century photograph and tell who the photographer is. You certainly can't do that today. It isn't only the camera and lens, but also the type of film (or in those days, glass plate), the developer used and how the print is made onto particular types of paper. Each gives a distinct interpretation".

John Grace - email - 18/06/25

The Trust looks forward to welcoming architects, designers, graduates, students and interested members of the public to attend this event and support the Trust in its work.

The Futuna Trust is a charitable organisation and all koha received from the exhibition events will go towards the ongoing care, maintenance and operation of Futuna Chapel and also to support various initiatives undertaken by the Trust.  Please register

REGISTRATION IS PREFERRED TO ATTEND THIS EVENT. Note that the sunday exhibition hours are 11:00am to 2:00pm. This allows for the public talks that commence at 2:00pm.

long_description:
Ever wondered what it really takes to make it to the top? Join us for an evening of speed networking with some of Wellington’s most inspiring executives.

At Get to Know a CxO, you’ll have the chance to move around the room and chat one-on-one with a range of senior leaders. Expect candid conversations about their career journeys, lessons learned, and the moments that shaped their leadership.


This isn’t your typical panel event. It’s relaxed, interactive, and designed to help you connect directly with the people behind the titles. Whether you’re curious about leadership, thinking about your next move, or just love hearing great career stories, this event’s for you.

Come for the insights, stay for the connections ✨

📅 Thursday 3rd December, 5:00PM for a 5:30pm start

📍 Venue: KPMG - Level 6, 44 Bowen Street, Wellington

🎙️ Speakers: 

Philip Whitmore, Partner - Cyber at KPMG

Camy Bhandari, Co-Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

Tristan Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Databricks

Additional speakers TBC.

Spots are limited, with FLINT members taking priority over non-members so register now to secure your spot!

FLINT is free to join, please register here: https://tuanz.org.nz/flint-signup/

We look forward to seeing you there.

_______________________

About FLINT

If you’re in the early stages of your career and you’re interested in digital technologies, come join the FLINT programme in your local city. We host events, webinars, podcasts and social catch ups that offer valuable networking, learning and growth opportunities. 

Find out more about the Wellington FLINT team here.

	

	




 

	

Philip Whitmore, Partner, Cyber and Digital at KPMG

	

Philip is a Partner within KPMG Cyber with over 30 years’ experience across a broad range of cyber security disciplines. He has worked extensively in New Zealand, as well as throughout the wider Asia Pacific region.  His cyber security knowledge and experience is supported by his wider business consulting background, giving him the ability to readily translate cyber security risks into a business context. Philip’s experience saw him win the New Zealand Cyber Security Person of the Year award in 2023.




	

Tristana Leist Bessler, Public Sector Account Manager at Data Bricks

	

Tristana Leist hails from Databricks, working with Aotearoa organisations to explore how data and AI can support better services and decision-making. Joining us from Seattle, WA, her work has spanned government, defence, education, and aerospace. She leads digital transformation with joy... and the occasional tap dance routine.

Tristana also just scooped up the TUANZ Member awards for 'Outstanding Future Leader'.




	

Camy Bhandari, Co Founder & Director at NZ Tech Rally

	

Camy Bhandari is the Co-Founder and Director at NZ Tech Rally, a community platform for tech practitioners in Aotearoa New Zealand. NZ Tech Rally brings tech professionals from across the country together to build a more diverse, equitable and inclusive tech industry through conferences, meetups and workshops.

She brings over 16 years of software development experience across banking, fintech, consultancies, startups and government. As a first-generation migrant, woman of colour and neurodiverse person, Camy draws on her own experiences to shape NZ Tech Rally into an inclusive and accessible space for everyone.

long_description:
We’re bringing our Wellington community together for a relaxed evening of conversation and connection. This is less about formal presentations and more about meeting others in the HealthTech community, sharing experiences and learning from one another.

As part of this catchup, two of our members will share their career journeys, the different pathways that brought them into digital health and some of the lessons they have learned as women working in the industry. Come along for a drink, an open conversation and the opportunity to connect with people who understand the opportunities and challenges of working in HealthTech.

What to expect

5.00 pm-5.30 pm: Arrive, grab a wine and meet others from the Wellington HealthTech community

5.30 pm-6.30 pm: An informal member spotlight and conversation with Catherine Epps and Jennifer Anderson

Meet our speakers

Catherine Epps is Director, Medical Devices at Pharmac, a role she has held since 2023. The range of medical devices used across the public health system is vast, with technology playing an increasingly important role in how many of these devices function. Catherine has more than 20 years’ experience in senior leadership roles across public and private healthcare organisations in Aotearoa, including serving as Executive Director Allied Health, Scientific and Technical at Capital & Coast District Health Board. She later led a broad portfolio at WorkSafe focused on reducing work-related health harm, including carcinogens, mentally healthy work and musculoskeletal harm.

Originally trained as a speech-language therapist, Catherine is a Fellow of the Australasian College of Health Service Managers and a Chartered Director. She is currently Board Chair of Stroke Aotearoa New Zealand.

Jennifer Anderson works in biotech commercialisation, with a focus on technologies that improve human health. Her career spans New Zealand’s public and private sectors, including roles in technology transfer offices, early-stage investment firms and start-up companies. This experience has given her a practical understanding of what it takes to move science from the laboratory to the market, from intellectual property management and financing to building the right team. Jennifer is currently Business Development and Commercialisation Manager at the Malaghan Institute of Medical Research, where she helps identify promising innovations and supports their translation into the clinic.

Whether you’re well established in HealthTech, exploring a new direction or simply keen to meet others in the community, we’d love you to join us.

*Please note: if you arrive and the building doors are locked please call Nuala on 027 244 9692

id: tipsy trails #41 Wellington-74 Truscott Avenue, Johnsonville, Wellington 6037, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: tipsy trails #41 Wellington
venue: 74 Truscott Avenue, Johnsonville, Wellington 6037, New Zealand
long_description:
If you’re new here, welcome - stoked you found us!

We’re tipsy trails. We’re on a mission to get more people in their 20s outdoors and turn an online community into a seriously epic in-person one.

We walk together along some of New Zealand’s most stunning trails, chatting with new and old mates - usually wrapping things up with a well-earned beverage afterwards.

We’re a club built on the idea that getting outdoors doesn’t have to be super serious or intense - it should be accessible, with a bit of fun. You don’t need fancy gear. You don’t need to be “outdoorsy.” You don’t even need a group to come with - rocking up solo is totally normal here. All paces and abilities are welcome. You just need to show up and enjoy the rest.

So, what do you say? Put down your phone and come outside with us.

⛰️ TRAIL INFO

Trail: Skyline Track, Johnsonville

Length: Out & back (halfway), approx. 12km, 460m elevation gain, around 3 hours

Difficulty: Rated Moderate by AllTrails

🎒 WHAT TO BRING?

Water bottle (make sure it’s full!)

comfy walking shoes,

a warm layer for during and after the hike 🧥,

a waterproof jacket (just in case 🌧️),

trail snacks (interpret this however your heart desires),

hat, sunglasses, and sunscreen (fingers crossed for sunshine ☀️),

a bag to throw everything in (backpack or side bag works perfectly 🎒)

📍 MEETING POINT

Meeting details and timing will be emailed once you’ve registered.

Keep an eye on our Instagram and tipsy trails Facebook messenger group chats for any updates or weather changes.

🍻 POST-HIKE PLANS?

With the trail wrapped up and the afternoon still ahead, we’ll head to a nearby pub for a well-earned beverage and bite to eat!


🚙 NEED / CAN OFFER A LIFT

Carpooling is available for anyone who needs a lift or can offer one. Once you have registered, you can connect with others in the Facebook messenger carpool group chat, share your area, and organise pick-up details directly.

🥾 REGISTRATION

This is a free community event with limited spots. Registration is required.

Got questions? Our DM’s are always open on Instagram @tipsy_____________

id: Capital Blues Presents: BlueBerries-21 Blair Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: Capital Blues Presents: BlueBerries
venue: 21 Blair Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
long_description:
One of the great pleasures of Wellington's music scene is stumbling across exceptional talent when you least expect it. Earlier this year, a young group of musicians caught our attention while busking on Cuba Street. Their musicianship, energy and obvious enjoyment of playing together made an immediate impression.

A few months later, that chance encounter has become a Capital Blues debut performance.

For these emerging musicians, the journey has involved building a full-length set, refining their repertoire, and preparing for their first performance before a dedicated audience. It's exactly the kind of opportunity Capital Blues seeks to create; giving young artists a platform to grow their confidence, develop their craft, and connect with new listeners.

Join us in supporting what may well be the next generation of outstanding Wellington musicians. You might just discover your new favourite band before everyone else does.

Featuring:

Maddie Glossop - vocals

Noah Bryn - guitar

Oliver Livingstone - double bass

Reuben Stevens - drums

Georgina Willan - alto saxophone

long_description:
CLUEDUNNIT

DINNER WITH 'MURDER ON THE MENU'

Step into a world of intrigue, suspense, and unforgettable entertainment as InterContinental Wellington partners with Cluedunnit to present an immersive murder mystery dining experience. Guests will be transported into a captivating story where secrets unfold, clues emerge, and every guest becomes part of the investigation.

Combining exceptional hospitality with live theatrical entertainment, Cluedunnit invites guests to enjoy a delicious dining experience while questioning suspects, following leads, and working together to solve a thrilling mystery. From the moment you arrive, you'll be immersed in a world of drama, laughter, and unexpected twists.

Whether you're planning a unique night out with friends, celebrating a special occasion, or enjoying an unforgettable evening with colleagues, Cluedunnit at InterContinental Wellington promises the perfect blend of fine dining, mystery, and entertainment.

Guests will interact with a live cast of characters, uncover clues, and work together to crack the case, all while enjoying a delicious three-course dinner.

But beware, all is not as it seems. As secrets unravel and tensions rise, you'll need to decipher the clues, question the suspects, and piece together the evidence before it's too late. After all, where there's a will, there's a murder.

Where there's a mystery, there's a motive. Where there's a motive, there's a murder. The question is: whodunnit?

MURDER AT THE MANOR - The Story So Far...

It is 1929 and this English Cotswold beauty spot is celebrating the life of elderly heiress Rose Stimper, who, in an act of philanthropy, has bequeathed the village a large sum of money and left instructions that the villagers must decide how best to spend it. 

This will be a party like no other. Everyone has ideas on how to spend the money, and the entire village turns out to attend Pokeingham Hall, which has been thrown open for the first time in many years to host the event.

But beware, all is not as it seems. There are dark forces at work.

Enjoy a delicious three course dinner as you question the suspects, decipher the clues and work to crack the case. And please remember - where there’s a will, there’s a murder!


DINNER MENU:

STARTER: gf/v

Sashimi cut Akaroa salmon and yellow fin tuna, preserved lemon, harissa, coriander

MAIN COURSE: gf/v

Corn fed Chicken supreme, truffled portobello plin ravioli, ajo blanco, spring asparagus, chardonnay jus

VEGETARIAN MAIN COURSE: gf/df

Risotto prima vera Aged Acquerello rice, asparagus, green beans, peas, parmesan fondue

DESSERT: gf/v

Dark blood chocolate mousse, with raspberry and dark chocolate crumble.

We cater for all dietary requirements - please select the relevant option at checkout. 

BOOKING YOUR PLACE AT A TABLE: 

You will be seated around tables of 10. If it is likely that friends will be coming along too, it is best to book all your places at the same time to ensure you are all on the same table.

Please note, ticket sales will end 72 hours before the event. 

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION, CONTACT:

info@cluedunnit.com.au

cluedunnitwellington@ihg.com 




0450 511 945

id: In Conversation With: Kate Hawley-129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington 6022, New Zealand-Humanitix
name: In Conversation With: Kate Hawley
venue: 129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington 6022, New Zealand
long_description:
We have a very special event to close the year.

WIFT NZ is delighted to welcome Oscar and BAFTA-winning costume designer Kate Hawley.

This year, Kate has won the following awards for her contribution to Guillermo del Toro's Frankenstein (2025)

Academy Award for Best Achievement in Costume Design

BAFTA for Best Costume Design

Critics Choice for Best Costume Design

Costume Designers Guild Awards for Excellence in Period Film

Plus 19 other awards around the globe!

She also received multiple nominations for Best Costume for Lord Of The Rings: Rings of Power (2022) and Crimson Peak (2015).

To top it all off, she also received the inaugural Costume Designer of the Year Award from the British Fashion Council. 

Hawley has been praised for her "...meticulous construction, narrative sensitivity and ability to elevate character through custom-built textiles and silhouettes. ...she has built an international career across film, opera, theatre and ballet. Her credits span Crimson Peak and Pacific Rim to Suicide Squad, Edge of Tomorrow and The Hobbit. Her work has previously earned an Emmy nomination, a Costume Designers Guild Award and Saturn and Empire award" - (Fashion United UK)

Kate’s body of work speaks for itself. She’s another fantastic story of a career that started at home in Aotearoa and went global,

We’ll pick her brain (not in a Frankenstein way) about her career, her craft, and what it takes to build a whole world out of fabric, dye and attention to detail. Moderated by Robin Laing.

Date: Tuesday 17th November

Time: Drinks from 6pm | Talk 6:30-8pm

Location: Wētā Workshop Space, 129 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington

WIFT Members free, non-members $25. Drinks and nibbles provided.

venue: Steamship Building North Queens Wharf, 57 Customhouse Quay, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand  ·  Accessibility info
long_description:
Playtime for serious professionals.

A free community event where we get together, talk creativity and doodle around.

Our theme this month is Surprise. Creative breakthroughs are usually just happy accidents. We'll talk about setting the conditions for the unexpected to happen, and harnessing surprises when they strike.

This event is in-person at Cuckoo Emporium, 57 Customhouse Quay in Pōneke/Wellington.

What to expect?

a fun, low-stakes, judgement-free zone where we exercise our imagination muscles

the warmth of other people's creative energy

hands-on doodling time, with prompts and support to work through creative blocks

What to bring?

a notebook

pens/pencils/whatever you’d like to work with

your curiosity

(optional) specific ideas and questions you want to doodle around with — work-related or otherwise

Doodle Cafe is free, but spaces are limited. Grab your ticket today and invite your friends and colleagues.

We're generously hosted by the awesome team at Cuckoo — so enjoy the space and grab drinks and snacks on the night.
